item.title: Soulja Boy Warns France Unrest Should Put World Leaders On Notice
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Soulja Boy's France warning drew a class-politics joke as he urged governments to hear people squeezed by the cost of living.
item.content:encoded:
Soulja Boy called on world leaders to pay attention to France, warning that people struggling with the cost of living could only take so much before their anger boiled over.

The rapper weighed in on X on Sunday, saying rising prices had left everyday people working hard while barely getting by. “What’s happening in France is a wake-up call to the entire world,” he wrote.

His message prompted some wordplay in the replies. X user @emptystun wrote, “Crank that class consciousness,” turning the title of Soulja Boy’s breakout hit into a joke about his focus on working people.

The economic demands behind the French demonstrations were laid out by the CGT union ahead of Saturday’s mobilization. In its statement last week, the union backed calls for higher wages and pensions, lower prices and public services that met people’s needs. It said its members would join students, workers and retirees where conditions allowed. It also described access to health care as an essential right.

In a follow-up statement on Saturday, the CGT urged the government to negotiate with student and worker unions and address the demands through parliamentary debate. It also called for peaceful protests to continue, with higher pay, pensions and minimum social benefits among its demands.

The union estimated that nearly 800,000 young people, workers, unemployed people and retirees had joined gatherings across France that day. It framed the mobilization as part of a movement that had been building for several weeks.

Soulja Boy’s comments came just over a week after he floated a move into public service. AllHipHop covered his 2028 presidential tease earlier this month, when he said he was exploring how his work in music, business and technology could translate into that role.

FOX 5 Atlanta reported last week that he had identified economic opportunity, criminal justice reform, education and technology, including artificial intelligence, as areas of interest. At the time of that report, he had not announced a formal campaign, named a political party or released a detailed platform.

He closed Sunday’s post with an appeal to governments:

“Governments need to start listening to the people before frustration turns into chaos.”

item.title: Cardi B Found Missing Birkin Esmeralda After Studio Tip
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B shared the studio clue behind her missing Birkin Esmeralda, a day after she feared she had left the purse at a hotel.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B said last week that she found Esmeralda, the Hermès Birkin she feared she had left at a hotel. Her update pointed to a studio.

“UPDATE!! I found her!!!!” she wrote on X, quoting her earlier post about the lost bag.

A screenshot of a text exchange supplied the clue. “It’s in Kollin’s studio,” one message read. Cardi expressed relief in her reply. The other person said the bag should still be there and offered to bring it next time.

She had shared the loss with fans a day earlier. A fan had asked her to bring Esmeralda back out. In that post, the fan shared an old clip of the brown leather purse. Cardi responded that she had lost it and thought she might have left it behind at a hotel.

She described Esmeralda as the only bag she could not find and said she felt sad about the loss. AllHipHop’s earlier report covered that exchange. Her follow-up gave fans a far more hopeful account of where the bag had ended up.

Her love of rare bags had sent her on long hunts before. In a July 2023 Vogue feature, she joked that buying a bag had brought her to Paris while she attended the couture shows.

“I really came here to buy a Birkin bag,” she said. She added that she had spent two months hunting for one she could not find in the United States.

Her taste for those pieces also led to a business deal. Fashionphile named her its 2026 global brand ambassador on May 20. Its “Get Your Bag” campaign featured Cardi with pre-owned luxury accessories and paired shopping with resale.

She also chose a group of bags and other accessories from Hermès, Chanel and Goyard for the site. The company shot the campaign in New York City. It used both photos and video.

Sarah Davis, Fashionphile’s founder and president, said the rapper understood the value of those pieces. She said Cardi could help change how people thought about resale.

“I love a good bag, but I love a smart buy too,” Cardi said in the launch announcement.

item.title: Jadakiss’ Son Says He Hates Biggie’s “Ready To Die” Album Right In Front Of Biggie’s Son!
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Jadakiss' son Jae'Won shocks Biggie's son CJ Wallace by declaring his hatred for "Ready to Die," igniting a generational debate.
item.content:encoded:
What in the heck is going on?

Jadakiss‘ son Jae’Won might have committed a Hip-Hop felony by telling Biggie Smalls‘ son that he hates one of the most celebrated rap albums ever recorded. And he said it right to his face!

Now, I have heard some controversial opinions in my lifetime, but this one deserves a congressional hearing by the gods of Rap. Elders, where are y’all? Kiss, get ya boy!

During an episode of their “Silver Spoons” podcast, Jae’Won and Christopher “CJ” Wallace got into a spirited discussion about The Notorious B.I.G.’s legendary debut, Ready to Die. Jae’Won apparently had no reservations about criticizing the album that helped establish his podcast partner’s father as a rap icon.

“I hate the first album, not going to lie,” Jae’Won admitted.

Excuse me?

CJ was stunned.

“That’s wild,” CJ responded, before adding, “We might need a timeout on that one.”

Jae’Won wasn’t finished. He argued that Biggie’s second album, Life After Death, was a superior artistic achievement because it demonstrated greater maturity, stronger storytelling and more sophisticated production.

“The whole album (Ready To Die) is just very chaotic,” he said. “It’s not cohesive enough for me.”

Now, here’s where I have to intervene.

Ready to Die was released in 1994, when New York Hip-Hop was experiencing a renaissance. The album was grimy, cinematic, funny, disturbing and brutally personal. That chaos Jae’Won dislikes? Some might argue that was precisely the point.

Biggie was documenting the psychological turmoil of a young man navigating poverty, street life, ambition and impending superstardom!

And let’s remember something else. Without Ready to Die, there probably isn’t a Life After Death as we know it. Come on.

Jae’Won praised “Juicy,” “Big Poppa,” “One More Chance” and “Dreams,” suggesting those records would have been better suited for the second album.

He acknowledged Biggie’s excellence as an MC.

“The rapping on Ready to Die was dope as hell, but the songs overall were just like, I could have done without some of the songs,” he reasoned.

Listen, everybody is entitled to an opinion. Even when that opinion sounds like somebody walked into the Louvre and complained about the paintings. I think he’s too young and does not have any connection to the source material.

This is all generational! These are two sons of Hip-Hop royalty discussing the work of one of the genre’s greatest artists.

CJ defended his father’s debut, but Jae’Won stood his ground. MEH.

Let me try to be objective. Is Jae’Won hearing something the older generation refuses to acknowledge, or is he missing the historical point that made Ready to Die extraordinary? I think it is the latter.

What does Jadakiss think about all this?

Because I would pay good money to hear THAT conversation. What the…lol…or Tha Whut!

item.title: Kai Cenat Sets Japan Return With Ray For October 21
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kai Cenat's new trailer nods to the Tokyo meeting that brought Ray into his streams, ahead of their planned Japan return.
item.content:encoded:
Kai Cenat set an October 21 Japan stream with Ray, the friend he first met in the country in 2023. He rolled out the trip with a skit that nodded to their first chat on a Tokyo street.

The two-minute “Returning To Japan | Official Trailer” went up on Kai Cenat Live on Sunday. Its description sent fans to a scheduled stream called “RETURNING TO JAPAN W/ RAY.”

The skit played up car talk and a character dubbed “Bankroll Ray.” It also recalled their first chat at a Tokyo 7-Eleven. By the end, the script called for a flight back to Japan and “a little reset.”

In a GQ Taiwan interview last year, Ray looked back on that meeting in the summer of 2023.

Ray was on a school trip in Japan when he learned Cenat was streaming nearby. He followed clues from the broadcast to find him and asked for a photo. The encounter played out live for Cenat’s viewers. He told GQ he had only wanted a picture. He feared he might never get another chance to meet Cenat.

Ray told GQ he saw Cenat and the AMP crew as brothers. He said their bond off camera matched what fans saw on stream.

Cenat invited Ray to the United States to make content, then went to Taiwan himself. Local broadcaster FTV covered his visit with Ray in February 2024. They stopped in Taipei’s Ximending and Xinyi areas. Fans brought food and gifts as Cenat streamed his travels.

The pair also took their chemistry into a short film. They starred in the 2023 short “Global Pursuit,” an action comedy built around two cops and a sting. TV Guide’s cast listing credited Cenat as Miller and Ray as Shadow. The film drew on the “Rush Hour” setup made famous by Chris Tucker and Jackie Chan.

Ray later made room for Cenat in his GQ Sports “10 Essentials” appearance, released in March 2025.

“My next essential, Kai,” he said. He recalled meeting Cenat near a 7-Eleven in Japan. He summed up how far they had come: “here we are now.”

Their next shared stream is scheduled for Wednesday, October 21, on Kai Cenat Live.

item.title: Jalen Hurts’ Blood Clot Crisis Analyzed By Renown Pulmonologist Who Warns Of Fatal Risks
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Renown pulmonologist Dr. Carole A. Guy assesses Jalen Hurts' frightening diagnosis and life-threatening dangers and hopeful football outlook.
item.content:encoded:
Jalen Hurts‘ season-ending blood clot diagnosis has raised serious medical concerns in Philadelphia.  And a prominent pulmonologist hailing out of nearby Delaware told AllHipHop that the Eagles quarterback survived a potentially fatal complication.

Dr. Carole A. Guy, a renown, award-winning Board Certified Pulmonologist in internal medicine and pulmonary medicine, spoke exclusively with AllHipHop founder Chuck “Jigsaw” Creekmur about Hurts’ diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.

Her assessment was sobering, although she expressed considerable optimism about his recovery.

“It’s extremely serious,” Guy said during the interview. “What concerns us about DVT (deep vein thrombosis) is that blood clots in the deep veins can travel to the lungs. Unfortunately, he developed bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning blood clots affected both lungs. Pulmonary emboli can be fatal. Even DVT can become fatal if a clot travels to the lungs. This is a very serious medical condition.”

The Philadelphia Eagles and Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, released a statement explaining that the quarterback was initially diagnosed with superficial vein thrombosis in his left calf by specialists in London.

Deep vein thrombosis is a condition in which blood clots form in deep veins, typically in the legs. Doctors also discovered bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning clots were present in the blood vessels of both lungs.

Dr. Guy explained that pulmonary emboli can develop when blood clots break loose and travel through the bloodstream to the lungs, potentially creating a fatal obstruction.

One particularly important aspect of the diagnosis involves Hurts’ reported calf injury and subsequent international travel.

The Philadelphia Eagles traveled to London for an NFL regular-season game, requiring players and team personnel to make a lengthy transatlantic flight. During the trip, Hurts was evaluated by medical specialists who initially diagnosed superficial vein thrombosis in his left calf.

Guy addressed physical trauma and prolonged immobility during extended flights as additional risk factors for developing blood clots.

Although professional athletes generally have a relatively low risk of developing DVT, she explained that injuries, dehydration and lengthy travel can increase their vulnerability.

On fan, not an expert, expressed rage at the fact that QB1 for the Eagles flew to London.

“How do you fly a dude to London , make him play on no sleep. Then reveal he has a career threatening blood clot,” the fan asked AllHipHop.

However, Guy cautioned against drawing conclusions about the Eagles’ medical decisions without access to Hurts’ complete medical history and treatment timeline.

She emphasized that the quarterback could have developed DVT even without traveling internationally because an existing superficial clot can also be associated with an increased risk of deeper clot formation.

Another critical concern involves the treatment necessary to prevent additional complications.

According to the Eagles’ statement, Hurts will undergo anticoagulation therapy, commonly known as treatment with blood thinners.

Guy explained that anticoagulants help prevent existing clots from growing and reduce the risk of additional clot formation while the body’s natural processes gradually resolve the obstruction.

Unlike clot-dissolving medications used in certain severe cases, anticoagulants do not directly break apart existing blood clots.

The treatment also explains why Hurts cannot participate in contact football.

“Hurts is young, healthy and physically conditioned. His medical team has identified the problem and is treating it,” she said. “Based on the information available, his prognosis is excellent. The most important thing now is allowing him to recover and avoiding unnecessary risks while he’s receiving treatment.”

Players taking anticoagulants face an increased risk of serious internal bleeding following collisions, particularly injuries involving the head or abdomen.

Guy also discussed potential long-term complications associated with DVT and pulmonary emboli, including persistent shortness of breath, chest discomfort and post-thrombotic syndrome, which can cause ongoing leg pain and swelling.

Nevertheless, she emphasized that Hurts’ youth, physical conditioning and the absence of any publicly reported underlying cardiovascular disease are encouraging factors.

“His prognosis is excellent,” Guy said.

The Eagles similarly expressed confidence in Hurts’ recovery, stating that he is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations.

The organization expects him to remain involved with the team and continue conditioning while receiving treatment. His eventual return to contact football will depend on completing anticoagulation therapy and receiving medical clearance.

“Jalen’s progress is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition,” Nicole Lynn said. “More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.”

For Philadelphia, the absence of its franchise quarterback represents a significant setback. But Guy’s medical assessment places the football consequences in a much broader perspective.

Hurts has built his career around resilience and overcoming adversity. His latest challenge won’t be measured by victories, passing statistics or championships.

Dr. Carole A. Guy serves as the Immediate Past Chair of Region II for the National Medical Association (NMA). Region II of the NMA covers Delaware, Washington D.C., Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and West Virginia. She is also an adjunct faculty at Temple University.

Jalen Hurts is expected to play again.

item.title: Big30 Backs Pooh Shiesty As Gucci Mane Takes Shots On “1017”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Big30 urged fans to keep faith in Pooh Shiesty as Gucci Mane vented on "1017" and the rappers awaited their federal trial.
item.content:encoded:
Big30 backed Pooh Shiesty with a message of faith as both rappers fought the federal kidnapping and extortion case tied to Gucci Mane.

Big30 posted on his Instagram Story, urging fans to keep faith in the pair as they dealt with the case. He said their music still had clubs and arenas buzzing while they faced limits on their freedom.

“I’m on house arrest you in a cell,” he wrote. He added: “NEVER GIVE UP ON US WE GOD FAVORITE.”

Gucci Mane had aired his own grievances on “1017,” the closing track from his album Against All Odds, released October 16. He aimed the song at unnamed artists, saying he put money in their pockets and helped make them stars, only to watch them act self-made.

“Y’all owe me some respect,” he rapped.

Big30 did not mention Gucci Mane in the message or say it was a response to the track.

Their links to Gucci Mane took different paths. Pooh Shiesty joined his 1017 roster and became one of its best-known acts. Big30 built his career with Moneybagg Yo’s Bread Gang and N-Less Entertainment. His past releases also carried Interscope’s name.

Big30 still worked with Gucci Mane, including on “Shit Crazy.” He and Pooh Shiesty had also been close since childhood and made music together well before this case.

Nine men were charged in the case. Federal prosecutors alleged that a January 10 meeting at a Dallas studio about Pooh Shiesty’s contract became an armed takeover. They said Pooh Shiesty pulled an AK-style pistol and forced Gucci Mane to sign papers releasing him from his deal. He was on home confinement from a prior federal gun case at the time, according to the Justice Department.

The government alleged that cash and jewelry were taken from three victims. It accused Big30, born Rodney Wright Jr., of blocking the studio door so they could not leave.

Big30 also pleaded not guilty. His lawyers argued that prosecutors had overstated his role in the case.

Pooh Shiesty’s father, Lontrell Williams Sr., was also charged. An FBI affidavit alleged that he booked the studio and told his son the signed release needed a date. His defense disputed that he joined a kidnapping plot. He pleaded not guilty, and U.S. District Judge David Godbey ordered his pretrial release in May.

Pooh Shiesty, born Lontrell Williams Jr., has also pleaded not guilty. He remained jailed after Judge Godbey denied a second bid for release in July.

His lawyers raised a new issue in an October 15 motion. As AllHipHop reported, they said he spent 23 hours a day alone in his cell and faced limits on family visits.

His trial is set for February 22, 2027.

item.title: Blueface Debates Taking His Livestream Fans To Church With Chrisean Rock
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Blueface debated bringing his livestream viewers to church with Chrisean Rock after a chance encounter led to an invitation.
item.content:encoded:
Blueface had a Sunday church trip lined up with Chrisean Rock, but bringing his livestream audience along gave him pause.

The rapper talked through that decision on his Kick stream before the planned outing. A longer excerpt uploaded Sunday captured him explaining how a chance encounter gave him both an invitation and a place to worship, then asking viewers whether they wanted to come along.

Blueface said the invitation came from a man who approached them while they were getting corn. He wasn’t sure whether the man was a pastor or a deacon, so he stopped short of giving him a title.

“I’m a little conflicted with bringing you guys though. You guys want to go to church with me? It’s kind of weird,” he said.

Chrisean Rock appeared beside him as the conversation turned to getting ready and leaving on time. Blueface joked about her having a reason to wear her dress, while the pair worked through how long the drive would take.

His nerves went beyond having a camera in church. Blueface told chat he wanted to arrive once people were already seated so the entrance wouldn’t become a spectacle. He also acknowledged that it had been a long time since he’d been to church.

For Chrisean Rock, faith has already become part of her public music career. She performed “Yahweh” at Faith City Central in Maryland in March 2025, joined by gospel singers Tim Bowman Jr. and Arissa Divyne.

That appearance also gave her a chance to discuss her beliefs with the church’s leaders. She described her faith as a personal commitment and pushed back against people who questioned her motives for sharing it publicly.

The family’s church connection predates that performance. In September 2023, Chrisean Rock brought their son to a dedication service, where his middle name, Jesus, was revealed. Blueface publicly supported that decision at the time.

This weekend, he was still figuring out the streaming side. Blueface said he thought filming would be allowed because churches record services, but he didn’t present that assumption as permission from this church. He told viewers the outing was happening whether or not they joined the stream.

item.title: Lil Wayne Blasts NFL Refs On Packers-Cowboys Night
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lil Wayne ripped NFL refs in three Sunday-night posts. His Packers beat Dallas 23-13 in a game with 22 penalties.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Wayne blasted NFL referees in three quick posts on X after cheering on his Green Bay Packers, who beat Dallas 23-13 at Lambeau Field on Sunday.

On Sunday night, Wayne wrote: “NFL refs ain’t shit.” About 40 seconds later, he posted a second version: “NFL referees ain’t shit.”

Within three minutes of the first post, he added another blunt line: “They make it hard to watch fr.”

A few hours earlier, Wayne had posted “GO PACK GO!!!!” His later complaints came on the same night as Green Bay’s prime-time game against the Cowboys, though he did not name a game or point to a specific call in those posts.

The matchup had plenty of flags. The Packers’ official recap counted 11 penalties for 96 yards against Green Bay and 11 for 108 yards against Dallas. Five of the Packers’ penalties were personal fouls: two for taunting and three for roughing the passer.

Packers coach Matt LaFleur stressed the need to keep emotions in check, whether players agreed with the calls or not.

“You’ve got to control your emotions to the best of your ability.”

The flags did not keep Green Bay from its third straight win. The Packers took a 17-0 lead into halftime and improved to 4-2. Dallas dropped to 2-4.

The Cowboys’ account described an offense that struggled to find a rhythm. Dak Prescott threw two interceptions, while Green Bay converted nine of its 10 third-down chances in the first half. Jordan Love finished with 276 passing yards, one touchdown pass and a rushing score. Matthew Golden led Green Bay with six catches for 104 yards and a touchdown. Green Bay’s defense also stopped Dallas on two fourth-down tries in scoring range, helping protect the early lead.

Wayne’s public ties to the Packers reach far beyond one Sunday-night post. His “Green & Yellow” theme song put that support on record in 2021.

He added another chapter this season with “Special Ops,” a Packers anthem that took shots at the rival Chicago Bears. AllHipHop covered that release in August, when Wayne aimed bars at Bears coach Ben Johnson and other NFC North rivals.

item.title: Big Wic’s Journey From New Haven’s Streets to MTV and BET
item.dc:creator: Staff Writer
item.description: Connecticut rapper Big Wic continues his independent journey with “Cheesecake” and “Show Power,” earning national exposure on MTV and BET.
item.content:encoded:
The Connecticut rapper built his career through independent distribution, collaborations with Hip Hop veterans, and a catalog that continues to reach new audiences.

Before his music videos reached MTV and BET, Big Wic was helping move mixtapes through a record store in New Haven, Connecticut.

The rapper, born Anwar Marcus Shakur, wasn’t just trying to get his own records heard. He was building a business around the music, establishing connections with artists and DJs during an era when independent distribution could make or break a release.

Born in Philadelphia and raised in New Haven’s Jungle neighborhood, Shakur began his career performing as Wicked. His involvement in Connecticut’s underground Hip Hop scene dates back at least two decades. In 2006, he was featured in the opening pages of Street Confinement magazine, an early acknowledgment of his presence in the regional rap scene.

He eventually established Diamond Records, a New Haven storefront that served as a distribution hub for independent East Coast mixtapes. The business put him in a position to understand both sides of the industry, from recording music to getting it into circulation.

That experience carried over into Push Entertainment LLC, the company he established to manage his recordings, video production, and promotional activities.

From Connecticut to Hip Hop’s Inner Circle

Big Wic’s independent work also brought him into the studio with some familiar names.

His Lost Files mixtape series includes collaborations with Raekwon, Prodigy of Mobb Deep, and Papoose. The projects connected him with a generation of East Coast artists whose careers were closely tied to the same mixtape circuit that helped shape his own.

Among those relationships was his work with the late DJ Kay Slay.

The veteran DJ helped curate an installment of Lost Files, which was finalized for independent release after his death.

For Big Wic, the project became part of a recording history that stretches from Connecticut’s local Hip Hop scene to some of New York’s most recognizable voices.

“Cheesecake” and “Show Power” Expand His Reach

In 2026, Big Wic drew renewed attention with “Cheesecake” and “Show Power,” the latter produced by Young Taylor.

The singles marked another chapter in his independent career, with digital distribution through CD Baby and music video promotion handled by HIP Video Promo.

According to his promotional materials, the campaign secured music video rotation on MTV and BET, while Connecticut’s Hot 93.7 (WZMX) provided mixshow airplay support.

The placements introduced his recent work to audiences beyond the regional scene where he first established himself.

It’s a notable development for an artist whose career began when physical mixtapes, record stores, and DJ relationships were essential to independent promotion.

Today, Big Wic is operating in a considerably different industry, but his experience with distribution remains relevant. The tools have changed, and the audience is no longer limited by geography.

His career has taken him from distributing music through a New Haven storefront to releasing records through digital platforms and gaining national television exposure.

After more than two decades in Hip Hop, Big Wic is still adding to his catalog rather than relying solely on what he accomplished in the past.

item.title: E-40 Backs Valkyries As Too $hort & LaRussell Join WNBA Finals
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: E-40 backed the Valkyries on Instagram as Too $hort and LaRussell prepared to bring Bay Area rap to Game 2 of the WNBA Finals.
item.content:encoded:
E-40 backed the Golden State Valkyries on Instagram ahead of the WNBA Finals, while Too $hort and LaRussell prepared to join the team’s title run. The two rappers have roles in Game 2 on Monday night at Chase Center.

Last week, E-40 shared a reel with the Valkyries and Chase Center. The black-and-white clip mixed game footage with a courtside shot of the rapper. He exchanged a fist bump near the court.

“Tell us when to go. The Finals start tomorrow. See you there, Yay Area,” the caption read.

E-40 also attended Golden State’s October 9 win over the Aces in Las Vegas, the San Francisco Chronicle reported. The win clinched a Finals berth for a team in just its second year.

Too $hort has made the team part of his playoff plans, too. He praised its fans in a Sports Illustrated interview published after Saturday’s opener. He put the noise at Chase Center above the crowds at Warriors games.

“They’re not lying, like Ballhalla is louder. The fans are more intense,” he told the outlet.

E-40’s caption played off “Tell Me When To Go,” his 2006 track with Keak da Sneak.

Too $hort’s role has gone beyond hearing his own hits in the stands. He played halftime at Golden State’s first home playoff game in September. He has gone to every home playoff game since, Sports Illustrated reported.

For Monday’s Game 2, the San Francisco Chronicle reported that Too $hort was set to handle the pregame drum. Vallejo’s LaRussell was booked for halftime. Larry June played that slot at Saturday’s opener.

The three rappers share roots in the Bay’s sound. AllHipHop covered their roles in the 2023 podcast series “Remember the Time: The Hyphy Movement.” It traced the music, dance, slang and car culture that shaped the scene.

The Finals also changed the city’s rap calendar. Chase Center moved Doja Cat’s show with Latto from October 19 to October 25. The venue’s event page tied the move to Golden State’s Finals berth.

The Valkyries enter Game 2 up 1-0. They beat the Atlanta Dream 68-64 on October 17, led by Gabby Williams’ 26 points. The team’s official preview lists Monday’s tipoff at 5 P.M. Pacific, or 8 P.M. Eastern. USA Network and Peacock will carry the game.
